caption:
i've spent my life believing i had to be some kind of "finished product" before i could be seen, or that i had to be *more* than i was - more confident, more skilled, more beautiful, more fit, more intelligent, more well-spoken (the list was infinite)... 

what if "ready" isn't a place where we arrive, but a feeling we create through doing things *unready*? 

you're cordially invited to experiment with doing it UNready with me. 💕

#ready #realization #innermonologue
author: caro brooks
transcript: Oh, you don't find your voice and then share it. You find it through sharing it. Oh, I've had it backwards this whole time. I have spent nearly 40 years trying to do everything in the background, not letting anyone see me in process. Let me just go figure this out behind closed doors, whether that be like my own emotions or opinions or a particular skill that I wanna do. Let me get private lessons and then practice privately. No one can see me until I'm ready to be seen until I've met some kind of standard that I set for myself, some elusive, never reachable standard and just constantly tell myself, well, I'm not ready yet. What if you only get ready by doing it unready? So this is my experiment in doing it unready. This is my experiment in using my voice while I'm finding my voice, not after. There is no such thing as ready. There's no such place. This is the place. Come like experiment here with me. Come learn here with me. Come do it unready with me. I'm so tempted to just play a freaking piece on the piano right now just to show my process of being bad at something that I would like to be good at. Maybe I will.
title: You Find Your Voice By Using It
one_liner: There is no 'ready' — growth happens by acting before you feel prepared.
key_points: You don't find your voice first and then share it; you find it through sharing it
Waiting until you're 'ready' is chasing an elusive, never-reachable standard
Doing things 'unready' is the only real path to becoming ready
Progress requires letting others see you in process, not just the polished result
